releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.16
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.16 — cooldowns per quota pool

Background runs, `start`, `omp` and the permission model behave as in 0.9.15. This release changes how quota cooldowns are keyed.

## Changes

- **Cooldowns are kept per account and quota pool, not per model family.** Cloud Code bills two pools: every Gemini model draws on `gemini`, everything else on `other`. A cooldown recorded after `gemini-3.8-flash` ran dry now also holds for `gemini-4-carbon` and every other Gemini model on that account, instead of letting each family fail once before it learns. The other pool stays usable. `pool.json` keys are now `<name>|gemini` and `<name>|other`.
- **`--family <f>` still accepts any family.** `accounts cooldown record`, `accounts cooldown clear` and `accounts hold acquire` map the family you give to its pool, so existing callers keep working and may also pass `gemini` or `other` directly.
- **Cooldowns recorded by older versions move to their pool.** The first pool update after upgrading rewrites per-family keys to pool keys; families of one pool merge into the cooldown that ends last. Nothing to do by hand.
- **`accounts list` shows the pool.** The `COOLDOWNS` section and `--json` `cooldowns[].family` now carry the pool name.
- **Test fixtures never ask for a signature.** Fixture repositories set `commit.gpgsign=false`, so running the tests no longer asks a signing key (for example a hardware key) for a touch.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
```

No other step. A tool that records cooldowns for the shared pool, such as Switchblade, should be updated together with it so both sides use the same keys; an older one keeps working, but its cooldowns are then written under a family name that maps to the same pool.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.15
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.15 — transient omp extension and per-account concurrency

Background runs, `start`, and the permission model behave as in 0.9.14. This release changes the omp bridge, the installer, and account-pool scheduling.

## Changes

- **`agy-crew install` no longer installs the omp plugin.** The extension loader is no longer part of an install; the command now removes a loader that an earlier version wrote. A file the user put at `~/.omp/agent/extensions/agy-crew-omp.ts` is left alone.
- **The omp extension lives only as long as an `agy-crew omp` run.** The launcher writes the bundled extension before omp starts and removes it when omp exits, including after a refused or failed run. The old installed-extension check and `AGY_CREW_OMP_SKIP_INSTALL_CHECK` are gone.
- **`agy-crew omp` requires `--use-at-my-own-risk`.** Loading an installed extension into omp is not a supported omp interface and can break the session. Without the flag the command refuses before holding an account, writing a file, or launching omp. `--help` still works without it.
- **`accounts parallel <name> [<n>]` limits agent-dispatched runs per account.** Skill-driven runs (`staffer`, `research`, `review`, `implement`, `ask`, `continue`, `restart`) take one slot per account by default; the command raises that to 1–64 for one account without requiring it to be idle. `auto` picks an account with a free slot, and a run fails with reason `busy` when none is available. Interactive `start` and `agy-crew omp` still hold their account exclusively. A credential on loan is exclusive whatever the limit: neither lender nor borrower takes another run until the loan is restored, and a loan never starts while the borrower has another run lease. `accounts list` gains a `PARALLEL` column and `--json` includes `parallel`, so the caller can size a batch to the free slots.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

`install` retires the loader written by 0.9.14. Restart the harness, and restart any running `agy-crew omp` session. Existing `agy-crew omp` commands need the new flag:

```bash
agy-crew omp --use-at-my-own-risk work1 -- --model google-antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash
```

Existing pool accounts keep working with one slot each; raise a limit only when you want several jobs on one account.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.14
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.14 — omp bridge: install check and connection-drop retries

Background runs, account selection, `start`, and the permission model behave as in 0.9.13. Both changes are in the experimental `agy-crew omp` bridge.

## Fixes

- **`agy-crew omp` refuses to start without the omp extension.** Without the extension omp starts normally but never sees the pool account: `google-antigravity` stays paused and the session runs on whatever else is configured. The launcher now checks before it holds an account, and exits with the command to run when neither the loader written by `agy-crew install --hosts omp` nor the `omp plugin install agy-crew` package is present. A loader that points at a removed package (for example after switching Node versions) is refused the same way. Set `AGY_CREW_OMP_SKIP_INSTALL_CHECK=1` if you load the extension some other way, such as an omp `--profile`.
- **A dropped connection no longer ends the turn.** omp replays a failed turn only when the error text matches its transient-transport wording. A dropped connection to the Cloud Code endpoint surfaces as `EPROTO: The TLS handshake failed. Does the server speak TLS on this port?` (or a bare `ECONNRESET` / `EPIPE`), which that wording does not cover, so a single flaky connection ended the turn, sometimes with `Tool call was not executed because the provider stream ended with an error`. The extension now rewords these errors, for requests to the Cloud Code hosts only, both when the request is rejected and when the response stream breaks. omp's own retry budget (`retry.maxRetries`, 10 by default) then applies to them, as it already does to `503 No capacity available`. The extension does not retry by itself. Set `AGY_CREW_OMP_TRANSPORT_SHIM=0` to turn the rewording off.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness, and restart any running `agy-crew omp` session to pick up the new extension. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.13
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.13 — omp bridge and daily update checks

Background runs, account selection, `start`, and the permission model behave as in 0.9.12.

## What's new

**`agy-crew omp` (experimental).** Run omp on one held pool account:

```bash
agy-crew omp work1 -- --model google-antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash
agy-crew omp       -- --model google-antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash
```

`--` ends agy-crew's flags; everything after it goes to omp unchanged. The command selects a pool account, holds it until omp exits, and provides the bundled omp extension with the account's runtime credential. The extension takes back the paused `google-antigravity` provider, installs the credential as a runtime bearer (no `agent.db` write, no profile, no session restriction), rewrites block 0 to the agy-crew identity, and strips `cfg://` and `omp://` fingerprints from prompts and tool declarations. A background agy warm-up refreshes the bearer before expiry. `agy-crew install --hosts omp` installs the extension loader; the extension is inert when `AGY_CREW_OMP_ACCOUNT` is unset, so a plain `omp` is unchanged.

The bridge accepts only `auto` or a pool account. It never reads a live agy login, so there is no special `--account live` handling in the omp path.

**Daily npm update check.** Interactive `agy-crew start`, the full-screen `agy-crew inspect`, and the human-facing `accounts list` / `accounts quota` tables check the npm registry at most once per 24 hours. When a newer release exists they print a one-line update notice on stderr. The result is cached in `~/.agy-crew/update-check.json`.

The check requires a TTY and skips known coding-harness environments, so agent skill calls never check, wait, or write the cache. Machine-readable `--json` account output never checks. Set `AGY_CREW_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to disable it.

## Fixes

- **Credential refresh no longer waits for agy's print turn.** `agy` can refresh a file token in a fraction of a second and then keep the `-p` turn open much longer. The bridge and `accounts quota --refresh` now stop agy as soon as the token file changes, so `agy-crew omp` starts in seconds instead of appearing to hang for a minute.
- **The omp bridge raises Antigravity's first-event budget.** omp's catalog gives Gemini Flash a 60-second first-event timeout. A cold or loaded Gemini start can exceed it, and omp reports `Request was aborted` before any token arrives. `agy-crew omp` now passes `PI_STREAM_FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000` (an explicit user value still wins), matching the five-minute budget used for other providers.
- **The first request uses a valid credential.** The launcher resolves and caches the Cloud Code project, and the omp extension registers the cached account credential as a provider fallback before model discovery. The role default no longer briefly falls back to another provider, and `session_start` still installs the runtime bearer.
- The omp bridge no longer advertises or attempts live-account support; the bundled extension has no live branch.
- `agy-crew omp` takes the account as an optional first positional, matching `agy-crew start`; its usage text lists `[<name>]`.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. If you use the omp bridge, re-run `agy-crew install --hosts omp` (or a normal `agy-crew install`) to refresh the extension loader. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.12
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.12 — account rename, tab completion, skills in the shared home, inspect across worktrees

Background runs, account selection and cooldowns behave as in 0.9.11.

## What's new

**`accounts rename <old> <new>` and `accounts refresh-email`.**
- `rename` moves the account's directory, cooldowns, quota snapshot and conversation bindings to the new name. It refuses while the account is in a lease or loan, lends the shared session, or the new name is taken or invalid.
- `refresh-email [<name>...] [--json]` re-reads each account's email from its token file (offline; run `accounts quota --refresh` first to have agy renew the token) and updates the pool record. A missing token, a token without an email, or an email another account already carries is reported and the record is left alone.

**Tab completion.** `agy-crew completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a completion script. It completes commands, subcommands, flags, flag values (models, efforts, `--hosts`, `--family`), account names and job ids. `agy-crew install` sets it up for you (below).

**`install` puts the skills into the shared home.** The shared home (`~/.agy-crew/shared/home`) is the HOME that `start` and pooled runs give agy, so agy now finds the `agy-crew-*` skills there too. It is a new host, `shared` (`~/.agy-crew/shared/home/.agents/skills`), included in every default install without detection; `--hosts shared` selects it alone and `uninstall` removes it with the rest.

**`install` sets up shell completion.** The scripts go to `~/.agy-crew/completions/`. bash and zsh get one marked block in their rc file (`# >>> agy-crew completion >>>` … `# <<< agy-crew completion <<<`) that sources the script; the rest of the file is never touched and a repeat install replaces the block. fish gets `~/.config/fish/completions/agy-crew.fish`; a file you wrote yourself there is left alone and reported as a conflict. A shell is set up when its rc file exists or it is your login shell. `--no-completion` skips it, `--dry-run` writes nothing, and an rc file that cannot be written only warns. `uninstall` removes the blocks and files together with the last skill link.

## Fixes

- **`inspect` now sees jobs started in other worktrees.** Each git worktree keeps its own `.agy-crew/`, so an agent working in an auto-created worktree left its jobs where `inspect` in the main checkout could not see them. `inspect` now merges the jobs of every worktree of the repository (read-only): the Jobs page and status line mark jobs from another worktree with `[worktree-name]`, a bare `inspect` picks the newest job of any worktree, and `inspect <id>` finds it wherever it ran. `--here` restricts the view to the current worktree. A corrupt `state.json` in one worktree is skipped with a warning. `status`, `wait` and `result` still look at the current worktree only.

## Behaviour change

A default `install` now also writes to the shared home and to your shell's rc file (bash, zsh) or fish completions directory. Use `--no-completion` to skip the latter. If you ran an earlier version, remove nothing: the next `install` adds both.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Open a new shell for tab completion and restart the harness for the skills. No migration is needed.

agy's skill directory for the shared home follows its `.agents/skills` convention; check with `/skills` inside `agy-crew start`.
